summary: The root لحي (lHy) primarily refers to the jawbone and, by extension, the beard. It can also describe the act of shaving or trimming the beard, or striking someone on the jaw.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: : see a verse cited voce خَطَبَ. لَحَاهُ ٱللّٰهُ: see شَرَاهُ.
(S, Mgh,) and تلحّى بِعِمَامَتِهِ, (TA, art. عجر,) He wound a part of his turban under his lower jaw: (S, Mgh:) as also تَحَنَّكَ, q. v.
اِلْتَحَيْتُ اللَّحْمَ عَنِ العَظْمِ [ I peeled off the flesh from the bone ]. (O, K, in art. سلق.)

[not لَحًى ] The jaw-bone; (Mgh, Msb;) either upper or lower: (Msb:) and, in a man, (Msb,) the part on which the beard grows. (S, Msb, K.) And sometimes Either lateral portion of the lower jaw: see َقَنٌ, and الفَنِيكُ.
لِحْيَةُ التَّيْسِ : see ثِيلٌ. لِحْيَةٌ is sometimes, by a synecdoche, put for the whole person: see a verse cited voce خُنْثٌ.

Bark; and in particular the bark of a plant, or of a tree, of which ropes &c. are made. The لِحَآء of the date is [its Pulp, pulpy pericarp, or flesh; i. e.] the part that clothes the نَوَاة [or stone ]. (TA.) لِحَآءُ العِنَبِ [ The skin of grapes ]. (TA in art. شحم.)
لَوَاحِى الشَّيْبِ , for لَوَائِحُ الشيب, q. v.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
